analyst_view.overall: Early view: Hapoel Beer Sheva's 'home' game is played at the Rapid-Giulesti Stadium in Bucharest, as Israeli clubs must use neutral venues, so the usual home edge is largely gone. Hapoel (33rd, 1 point) have scored once in four games, while Juventus (5th, 10 points) may be close to a top-eight place by then, which could bring some rotation.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean higher: Juventus have scored 11 in four European games and Hapoel have conceded eight, including 0-4 at Union. Hapoel's attack has barely functioned (no goals in three games), so the goals should mostly come at one end, and three of them looks reachable.

corners.text: The numbers say 7.9 corners, which looks low for a game Juventus should dominate at a neutral ground. Hapoel are likely to defend deep, as they did in a 0-0 with Dinamo, which tends to produce blocked shots and corners, so I'd expect 8 or 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards. A one-sided game in front of a small neutral crowd usually stays calm, and I found nothing pointing to a heated night.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.8 shots. Juventus should take most of them; Spalletti rotating in a game he may not need would trim the number a little, but Hapoel's weak defence works the other way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target. Juventus have been efficient rather than high-volume and Hapoel's 2.9 looks generous for a side with one goal in four, so the two roughly cancel and I stay close to 9.
